title: (Re-)enable setting atomic radii in GUI via the local config
body:
Previously, it was possible to specify a custom radius for each atom through the \~/.ase/gui.py configuration file using `gui_default_settings['covalent_radii']`. However, this feature seems to have been disabled in 7d2b447882902b46296c063273b867ae94090cf7 and later deleted from the code entirely (although this does not seem entirely intentional, as the documentation and related code were not changed accordingly).

This MR adds said functionality back with slight tweaks to also allow the use of a dictionary format and element symbols for the configuration.

Closes: ase/ase#928

- [x] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
author: lempelto

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
In ASE 3.13.0 and before, the `covalent_radii` setting is supposed to be given in a list/tuple of 2-element lists/tuples (https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/3.13.0/ase/gui/images.py?ref_type=tags#L66-68), and the present documentation https://ase-lib.org/ase/gui/basics.html also follows this.
I therefore agree that it is reasonable to support this type.

I would suggest, instead of `hasattr`, it may be explicit to do
`if not isinstance(radii, dict):`.
In principle we can also do [`if not isinstance(radii, Mapping):`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping), but in the present case, `radii` should be simply read from the configuration file `~/.ase/gui.py`, and therefore we do not have to assume the abstract class.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer suggests replacing `hasattr` with `isinstance` for a more explicit and idiomatic type check, which is about code clarity and proper use of Python idioms.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests replacing `hasattr` with `isinstance(radii, dict)` or `isinstance(radii, Mapping)` — a concrete code change.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Maybe a matter of taste, I would prefer e.g.
```python
for key, value in _radii.items():
    atomic_number = key if isinstance(key, int) else atomic_numbers[key]
    self.covalent_radii[atomic_number] = value
```
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer suggests a cleaner, more readable refactoring of the loop logic for iterating over radii, which is a general code quality/readability improvement.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests an alternative implementation with a specific code snippet — a concrete refactor.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Let's use `@pytest.mark.parametrize` e.g.
```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'radii',
    [{'Cl': 5.0, 1: 3.0}, [[17, 5.0], ['H', 3.0]]],
)
def test_custom_radii(gui, radii):
    hcl = molecule('HCl')
    radius_scale = gui.images.atom_scale

    gui.new_atoms(hcl)
    gui.images.configure_radii(radii)
    radii = gui.images.get_radii(gui.atoms)
    assert radii[0] / radius_scale == pytest.approx(5.0)
    assert radii[1] / radius_scale == pytest.approx(3.0)
```
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer suggests using `@pytest.mark.parametrize` to follow pytest idioms and reduce test duplication, which is a Python/pytest-specific convention for writing parameterized tests.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests using `@pytest.mark.parametrize` with a specific code example — a concrete test refactor.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @lempelto for reviving the custom radius setting option!

I agree, this has been disabled maybe simply by accident, and it should be reasonable to reactivate this option.

I have left a few suggestions on the code. Also,

1. It would be nice if you have also `changelog` with `scriv`.
2. It might also be helpful for users if we update `doc/ase/gui/basics.rst`, specifically https://ase-lib.org/ase/gui/basics.html#defaults, like
```rst
  gui_default_settings['covalent_radii'] = [[29, 1.6]]  # or {29: 1.6}
```
Then I think this MR will be ready to be merged.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer requests documentation updates (changelog and user-facing docs in `basics.rst`) to clarify the new feature for users, primarily a documentation/comment concern.
